resources.string: Clues, not certainty. A clean scan cannot rule out cameras.

Begin with what you can see. Work through the places below and save what you notice. Each tool collects clues for you to check yourself.
Focus on objects with a view of beds, showers, toilets and changing areas. Open a place for guidance, then mark it once you have looked.
Nothing here can confirm a hidden camera or prove a room is clear. Start with a visible webcam to learn how reflections behave.
Look at the face and grille for a tiny dark opening that points into the room. Use the camera with the light on from a few angles.
Check displays and grilles, especially on devices that face the bed.
Inspect USB adapters, power strips and outlets that face the bed or shower. Look for a small dark dot or an adapter that seems out of place.
Check front panels and status-light windows. Run a nearby scan: network equipment may answer discovery requests.
Look at corners and edges for holes, gaps or wires. Check behind frames that can be moved safely.
Inspect bases, shades and fixtures for a small lens or unexpected wiring.
Check small objects with a clear view of the bed, shower or changing area.
Look at the front panels and vents of devices that face the room.
Shine the camera light along vent slats and into corners. Look for a round dark opening that reflects the light.
Check hooks, holders, toiletries and anything that faces the shower or toilet.
Everyday items can hide a lens. Check those placed with a view of private areas.
Run a nearby scan and review the leads. Compare with what you expect, such as the room\'s Wi-Fi and your own devices.
Photos, readings and notes you save from these tools are linked to this place.
A strong magnetic change near an object that should contain no electronics, such as a book, frame or soft toy, is worth a closer look. Metal and magnets cause changes too.

resources.string: Turn on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Android Location. Connect to the room\'s Wi-Fi to check devices on its network. Allow precise Location when asked.
Compare with devices you know. These are advertisements and replies, not a list of cameras. Offline cameras may emit nothing.
READY · Tap Start scan to begin
Names, services or device descriptions that cameras commonly use. A lead is a reason to look closer, not proof. Many cameras show no lead, and ordinary devices sometimes do.
Nothing advertised a camera-like name, a video service or a video device role. That does not mean the room has no cameras: wired, offline or quiet cameras show nothing here.
Android normally limits foreground Wi-Fi scans to four per two minutes, and results can be cached. Devices connected to a network, including most cameras, never appear in this list.
Only devices that advertise appear. Names and signal strength do not establish identity.

Walk slowly around the room, holding the phone the same way. A stronger signal usually means a closer device or a clearer path; walls, bodies and reflections change readings. This is a direction to search, not a distance.
These measurements add context. None of them can identify a camera.
Compare the field near an object. Metal and magnets also change the reading; this cannot identify a camera.
Check which hardware streams are available and whether readings change.
Observe high-frequency tones. There is no universal camera sound signature.
Move away from metal, chargers and magnets. Tap Set baseline and hold still for at least 3 seconds. If accuracy is low, move the phone in a figure-eight, then retry.
Move close to the object, then away. Repeat. A change tells you the magnetic field changed, not what caused it.
Magnetic field is not radio signal strength. Ordinary metal and electronics can produce large changes.
Most useful on objects that should contain no electronics, such as books, frames, soft toys or tissue boxes. A change there suggests metal, magnets or electronics inside.

Every sensor exposed by Android is listed below, including unavailable or restricted streams. Light, proximity and motion help guide your sweep. Barometer and activity data provide context only. Fingerprint hardware and camera-internal autofocus/spectral sensors have no general raw sensor stream. NFC and GPS do not identify hidden cameras.

This deletes every inspection, photo, note and cached report on this device. Copies you already shared are not affected.

Camera frames and microphone samples stay in memory unless you save a photo. Saved photos, notes and readings stay in app-private storage. A nearby scan sends standard discovery requests on your Wi-Fi network but never connects to devices. Sharing uses the app you choose. No accounts, analytics, ads or cloud detection.
Designed for Pixel 9; adapts to other Android devices. Development-signed release. Hardware behavior still needs testing on a real Pixel 9. This app cannot guarantee a room is free of hidden cameras.

These observations were collected with a phone. They are clues, not proof: LensGuard cannot confirm a hidden camera or show that a room is camera-free. Reflections, metal, magnets and ordinary radios produce many of these signals.
Places inspected: %1$d of %2$d. Marked for a closer look: %3$d. Observations: %4$d. Photos: %5$d.

Camera: small bright points in the live view are marked, and a light on/off comparison separates reflections of the phone\'s light from light sources. Nearby: Wi-Fi access points, Bluetooth LE advertisements, and devices on the connected Wi-Fi network that answered standard ONVIF or UPnP discovery or advertised RTSP, HTTP or ONVIF services; names are compared with words that camera products commonly use. Magnetic: change in field strength from a still-phone baseline. None of these methods has a measured detection rate.
